name: Image Complexity
description: More complex images (e.g., higher texture, more objects, low contrast) are harder for *both* humans and the onboard classifier. This is the most likely driver of bimodality – certain waypoints reliably produce simple images, others complex.

name: Object Class
description: The onboard classifier may be significantly better at recognizing certain objects than others. A bimodal distribution could arise from images containing primarily 'easy' objects versus those containing 'hard' objects. Humans may also find some object classes easier/faster to verify.

name: Lighting Conditions
description: Poor or unusual lighting (e.g., direct sunlight, shadows, haze) affects both human and algorithm performance. This can drastically change image features and introduce noise.

name: Distance to Target
description: As the UAV gets further from the target, image resolution decreases. This can lead to more difficulty for *both* the classifier and the human, potentially creating a clear distinction in processing times.

name: Zoom Level/Field of View
description: The zoom level selected affects the details captured in the image. A narrow field of view might focus on a complex part of an object, while a wider view provides context but lower resolution.

name: Classifier Confidence Threshold
description: The internal confidence threshold the classifier uses to determine a 'successful' analysis might be leading to retries for images near the boundary, artificially skewing the distribution. The operator might be seeing only the borderline cases.

name: Waypoint Type
description: Different waypoints might be associated with different types of targets or environments. For instance, urban waypoints might have more complex scenes than rural ones.

name: Image Motion Blur
description: UAV movement or wind can cause motion blur, degrading image quality. Blurring makes it harder for both humans and computers to process the image.

name: UAV Speed
description: Faster UAV speeds may increase the likelihood of motion blur, especially if the camera's shutter speed isn't adjusted accordingly.

name: Wind Speed
description: Strong winds can affect UAV stability and increase motion blur.

name: Classifier Training Data
description: The onboard classifier’s performance is limited by its training data. If the training set doesn’t adequately represent all scenarios, it will perform worse on unseen scenarios.

name: Time of Day
description: Changes in light intensity and angle throughout the day can impact image quality and algorithm performance.

name: Operator Fatigue
description: The human operator's analysis time might vary depending on their fatigue level or attentiveness, though this is less likely to produce distinct *groups* and more likely to cause general variance.

name: Sensor Calibration
description: Improper or drifted sensor calibration could lead to image distortions or inaccuracies impacting both the classifier and the human's interpretation.

name: Atmospheric Conditions (e.g., fog, rain)
description: Visibility-reducing atmospheric conditions degrade image quality.
